`_write_archive` binds `size` inside one `if on_bytes is not None:` block and reads it in a second identical block after `tar.add`, so `size` is conditionally bound. Simpler: a `_input_size(path) -> int` helper (lstat, `st_size` if `S_ISREG` else 0), with `size = _input_size(file_path) if on_bytes is not None else 0` before the add and one guarded `done += size; on_bytes(done)` after it

No test pins the post-join drain in the cancellation branch. Every cancellation test has already queued its events before the drain at the top of the loop, so deleting this drain would leave the suite green. If that happens, an event whose put completes while workers are joining arrives after its label's cancellation result, and the label reappears in the live status.

The `self._on_progress is not None and not self._dry_run` guard in `_drain_progress` is half redundant. `_execute` passes `progress=None` under those conditions, so the queue is never filled. Only the None check (needed for mypy) is required

The PRD gives `Runner.__init__` one new kwarg, `on_progress`, and lists no new exports. The implementation also adds `on_tick`, which the CLI uses to refresh elapsed time when no events arrive. The PRD requires that refresh but names no way to do it, so this is a PRD gap closed with an unlisted parameter.
reason: single-voice; reviewed design explicitly defines optional on_tick to satisfy the PRD idle elapsed refresh

issue: The final catch-up `archiving` event in `on_finalize` ignores the 0.2 second throttle. Two further `archiving` events can therefore arrive less than 0.2 seconds apart; a test asserts a 0.1999 second gap. The spec text says at most one per 0.2 seconds, but the PRD happy path requires `done_bytes` to end at the total. The excess is at most one event per archive.
reason: single-voice; reviewed design explicitly requires final cumulative flush to retain final input bytes

issue: The progress queue is bounded (`maxsize=256`) and `_enqueue_progress` blocks until a slot frees. The PRD names only a plain `queue.Queue` and says progress can never fail an archive. A blocked put does not fail the archive, but it can stall the writer. This happens when the consumer holds a yielded result and does not iterate, for example when TTY output is paused with Ctrl-S.
reason: single-voice; reviewed design specifies bounded cancellation-aware backpressure and excludes consumer-held yields from tick timing
